Government decisions draw on research from many places. Universities and research institutes carry out studies, funders pay for them, statistical services publish data, advisory bodies weigh up the findings, and government departments, the Oireachtas and local government ask for and use the results. This map shows those organisations and the main routes along which money, requests and evidence travel between them.

Each large circle stands for a group of similar organisations, such as government departments or higher education institutions, and the small dots around it are the members of that group. Lines show four kinds of relationship. Select any circle or dot to see its members, its links and any figures attached to it.

## What the links mean

Research funding is money for research, for example from Research Ireland or the Higher Education Authority to universities. Demand for evidence is a request for research or analysis, usually from government. Supply of research-based evidence is research, data or analysis passed to the people who asked for it or who can use it. Evidence synthesis and advice is the step where findings are weighed up and turned into advice for decision makers.

## About this map

This is a working draft. It is redrawn from a map of the Irish evidence-policy ecosystem built with the Participatory System Mapper, and the groups and organisations follow that map. Some links in the original could not be traced with confidence and are left out until they are checked. The organisations, links and figures are kept in plain data files ([organisations](nodes.csv), [links](links.csv), [figures](stats.csv)) so the map can be corrected and extended.
